chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Kūfī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Mīthamī, from al-ʿAbbās ibn Hilāl al-Shāmī, a mawla of Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (عليه السلام), who said:
I heard al-Riḍā (عليه السلام) saying: Whenever the servants introduce sins that they had not been doing, Allah introduces for them afflictions that they had not been knowing.

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: introduced or brought about something new
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Imam al-Riḍā (عليه السلام), the speaker of the hadith
key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah, the One who decrees consequences and afflictions
key_terms.الْبَلَاءِ: affliction, trial, or calamity sent upon people
key_terms.الْعِبَادُ: the servants of Allah, meaning human beings morally accountable before Him
key_terms.يَعْرِفُونَ: they know or recognize, indicating unfamiliar forms of affliction

ai.seo_question: How do new sins lead to new afflictions according to Imam al-Riḍā (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the emergence of new forms of sin among people is met with new forms of affliction from Allah. It underscores a moral and theological link between collective wrongdoing and divine trial, warning believers against normalizing unprecedented sins.
